title: Alesia: Caesar Besieged Inside His Own Siege
summary: Recounts how in fifty-two BC the Arvernian chieftain Vercingetorix, who had united Gaul against Rome, shut himself up on the hill of Alesia with eighty thousand men, and how Julius Caesar built two rings of fortifications, one facing in and one facing out, then fought the huge Gallic relief army from between those two lines. The episode ranges from the defeat at Gergovia to the Mandubii left to starve between the walls, from the final assault at Mont Réa to Vercingetorix throwing his arms at Caesar's feet, to his strangling after the triumph in Rome, and to the dispute over the site that has gone on since Napoleon the Third's excavations in the eighteen sixties.
